The conductor is

\[
\boxed{\ \{f\in A:fB\subseteq A\}=A_+^{\,\left\lceil\frac{n-1}{r}\right\rceil-2}\ }.
\]

Let

\[
E=\{0,\dots,r\}\cup\{n-r,\dots,n\}.
\]

A degree \(d\) monomial of \(A\) has the form \(s^{nd-J}t^J\), where \(J\) lies in the \(d\)-fold sumset \(S_d=dE\). If exactly \(i\) of the \(d\) chosen summands come from the upper block, then the possible \(J\)'s form the interval

\[
I_{d,i}=[\,i(n-r),\; in+(d-i)r\,].
\]

Hence

\[
S_d=\bigcup_{i=0}^d I_{d,i}.
\]

The gap between consecutive intervals \(I_{d,i}\) and \(I_{d,i+1}\) has size controlled by

\[
(i+1)(n-r)-\bigl(in+(d-i)r\bigr)=n-(d+1)r.
\]

Thus \(S_d\) is the full interval \([0,dn]\) exactly when

\[
n-(d+1)r\le 1.
\]

Now a degree \(d\) monomial \(s^{nd-J}t^J\in A_d\) is in the conductor iff multiplying by every degree-one monomial of \(B\) remains in \(A\), i.e.

\[
J+q\in S_{d+1}\qquad\text{for every }0\le q\le n.
\]

This holds for every \(J\in S_d\) exactly when \(S_{d+1}\) has no gaps, namely

\[
n-(d+2)r\le 1
\iff
d\ge \left\lceil\frac{n-1}{r}\right\rceil-2.
\]

If \(d\) is smaller, then \(S_{d+1}\) has a genuine gap, and every interval \([J,J+n]\) meets such a gap, so no nonzero degree \(d\) element lies in the conductor.

Therefore the conductor consists precisely of all homogeneous pieces of \(A\) in degrees

\[
d\ge \left\lceil\frac{n-1}{r}\right\rceil-2.
\]

Since \(A\) is standard graded, that is exactly

\[
\boxed{A_+^{\,\left\lceil\frac{n-1}{r}\right\rceil-2}}.
\]
